type Both = A + B is a transparent alias, so with !Both has to forbid
both members — otherwise a named capability set is a hole in the
negation, and a developer naming a set is exactly when the medium should
keep proving absence. leak-alias-negation performs A under !Both:
refused. sound-alias-negation performs C, which the alias does not name,
under !Both + C: accepted. The pair pins both failure directions, since
a negation that under-refuses leaks and one that over-refuses makes
named rows unusable.

mentl/353af0f:
The binary refuted the §4① hypothesis: a ++ [1,2] grounds (list_concat), and a
concrete-init fold([9], …) floors identically to fold([]). So ++ propagates from
a known operand; the gap is that fold's accumulator (init, a handler-state value)
never grounds the lambda's acc param. map works because its config-f is applied
to the payload element (grounds via the position-wise flow); fold applies f to
the state accumulator, and that link is missing — the frozen-handle / order-free
class, exposed by dissolving infer_seq_op's seq_force. Not §4①, not an emit floor.

tokensafe/3508491:
Four fixes from consumer audit of live production. TRUMP scored 10 (LOW) when real risk is ~50 (HIGH) because Helius free tier fails getTokenLargestAccounts on high-holder-count tokens.

- Backup RPC fallback: BACKUP_RPC_URL env var (e.g. Alchemy free tier). Primary fails → retry once → fallback. Both fail → UNAVAILABLE as before.

- top_holders uncertainty penalty +10 → +20. All-degraded max score 38 → 48 (HIGH — honest signal that missing concentration data is dangerous).

- trusted_authority: boolean on /v1/check/lite. True when active authority belongs to known issuer (Circle, Tether). Agents understand why risk is LOW despite authorities_renounced=false.

- score_reliable: boolean on /v1/decide. False when degraded. Clear signal not to trust risk_score.
tokensafe/358c779:
getTokenLargestAccounts for high-holder tokens like TRUMP takes ~3s locally
and can exceed the 10s RPC timeout on Railway. The timeout error doesn't
match "Too many accounts" so DAS fallback was never triggered, leaving
top_holders UNAVAILABLE despite working DAS data.
noodles/35ad115:
Three complaints, three roots, one pass.

The mix read flat because 65% of rolls arrived bone-dry - nothing shared
a space. The dice still owns the sends (D9) but now rolls a depth floor:
small room on pad/lead (-20..-16 dB), a breath on drums (-27..-23), the
deep-wet third unchanged on top, bass never. The verb return takes 20 ms
of pre-delay so the room reads as depth behind the mix, and three static
carve filters do phone-speaker translation: bass +2 dB peaking at 900 Hz
(the note lives in harmonics on a driver with no fundamental), lead
+1.8 dB shelf at 2.6 kHz, pad -2 dB at 320 Hz. A full-mix saturator was
considered and skipped - the D7 ceiling already gives every path the
shared nonlinearity. Ratified as D17. Receipts: calibrate master row
holds a 0.9 dB rms spread across six combos, per-preset rms tight per
track; audit program -10.9 LUFS at -1.2 dBTP, six end-to-end rolls
inside 1.5 LUFS, all true peaks under -1.6.

Performance got worse with every dice roll because the voice pools only
ever grew: voice GC is deliberately disabled (its churn on sparse lanes),
so each roll's retrigger burst left ~13 more live oscillators with
forever-running param ConstantSources, plateauing only when all twelve
layer pools hit their caps. A boundary-time trim (after each roll, and
1.8 s after stop) mirrors the GC body once: CDP census shows the settled
graph at 1242 nodes after 12 rolls where it was 2102 (boot is ~1335).
Undo was exonerated - song snapshots measure ~3 KB.

Bass clip notes were engraving five ledger lines under the roll staff
canvas and clipping off it. The bass staff now follows the bass-guitar
convention - written an octave above sounding, sub-8 numeral under the
clef - so a rolled E1 sits one ledger under the staff, on the canvas.
